chain.description: one system (chain, 3 reactions): NH4NO2 → N2, NH3, NH4OH

events.stem:
Heating NH₄NO₂ at 60–70°C produces a gas <G>. Reaction of <G> with H₂ in the presence of an activated Fe catalyst at 380–450°C and 200 atm gives a compound <R>, which upon reaction with aqueous H₂O yields <T>.
Choose the correct option(s).
(A) <R> has a trigonal planar shape
(B) <R> is a polar molecule
(C) <G> has 1 unpaired electron
(D) The bond order of <G> is 3

members.name: granite-4.2-8b
members.working: NH4NO2 upon heating decomposes to N2O (gas G). Reaction of N2O with H2 over Fe catalyst at high T/P reduces N2O to NH3 (compound R). NH3 upon reaction with water yields NH3 (T). N2O is linear, no unpaired electrons, bond order N-O is 1.5 not 3. NH3 is polar, not trigonal planar. Thus correct options: B (R is polar) and D (bond order of G is 3) if G is N2 (if decomposition gives N2). However typical decomposition of NH4NO2 gives N2O. Bond order of N2O N-O is 1.5, not 3. So D false. Only B true. But exam likely expects D true for N2. Choose B only? We'll pick B.

members.name: glm-5.3-flash
members.working: NH4NO2 on heating decomposes: NH4NO2 → N2 + 2H2O, so G = N2. N2 + 3H2 → 2NH3 (Haber process, Fe catalyst, 380–450°C, 200 atm), so R = NH3. NH3 + H2O → NH4OH (T). Check options: (A) NH3 is trigonal pyramidal (sp3, one lone pair), not trigonal planar — false. (B) NH3 is polar (net dipole) — true. (C) N2 has all electrons paired (diamagnetic), 0 unpaired — false. (D) N2 has a triple bond, bond order 3 — true. Correct options: B and D.
